name: Tabitha
title: The Compassionate Disciple from Joppa
summary: Tabitha, also known by the Greek name Dorcas, was a Christian disciple in Joppa who was known for her generosity and good deeds, especially toward widows and the poor. She is best known for being raised from the dead by the apostle Peter, which led many to believe in the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Tabitha Presented as a Believing Disciple
keyEvents.description: Tabitha is introduced as a disciple in Joppa who was full of good deeds and acts of mercy. She was known for her care for the poor and needy in the church.

keyEvents.title: The Death and Preparation of Tabitha
keyEvents.description: Tabitha became ill and died. Her body was washed and laid in an upper room, in accordance with Jewish custom.

keyEvents.title: The Disciples Send for Peter
keyEvents.description: Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples sent two men to Peter with an urgent plea that he come to them without delay.

keyEvents.title: The Widows Show Tabitha's Deeds
keyEvents.description: When Peter arrived, he was taken up to the room where Tabitha lay. All the widows stood weeping around him, showing him the tunics and robes that Tabitha had made for her while she was still alive.

keyEvents.title: Peter Raises Tabitha from the Dead
keyEvents.description: Peter asked everyone to leave, knelt down and prayed, then turned to the dead body and said: "Tabitha, get up!" She opened her eyes, saw Peter, and sat up. He reached out his hand and helped her up.

keyEvents.title: Many came to believe because of the miracle
keyEvents.description: The news about Tabitha's resurrection spread throughout Joppa, and many came to believe in the Lord as a result of this powerful miracle.
